originalFindings.title: Negative-scope label definition supplies the form-to-answer mapping
originalFindings.actualClaim: The instruction asks learners to locate negation and read its effect; the ledger counts four complete-sentence scope interpretations.
originalFindings.evidence: Every instruction defines 外側 as 'uses はずがない to rule out the positive proposition as incompatible'. Testing for the literal substring はずがない selects 外側; otherwise selecting 内側 reproduces all four frozen answer keys. Thus the meaning distinction need not be independently interpreted.

reproduction.rule: Choose negation-outside when prompt contains はずがない; choose negation-inside otherwise.

originalFindings.impact: Useful form-location recognition is present, but the promised expectation-of-not-P versus rejection-of-P interpretation is supplied in the instructions. These are the only four new hazu-ga-nai scope tasks; legacy expectation tasks do not assess that missing distinction.
originalFindings.recommendedRemedy: Keep the same four items, IDs, readings and fixed answer-definition order. Define the labels by their meanings without naming the Japanese pattern that identifies the response. For example, contrast expecting the negative proposition to hold with ruling out the positive proposition as incompatible with the speaker's information. Recheck both modes and all feedback; no extra exercise quota is requested.
